channel.title: Enterprise on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Enterprise on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps generally available
item.description:
Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps are now generally available. This lets enterprises use GitHub Apps more broadly in place of classic PATs for automation, supported by an expanded API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Industry comparisons in the Copilot impact dashboard
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now adds an “Industry comparison” section. Enterprises and non-enterprise-owned organizations can compare their Copilot agentic adoption and leverage against aggregated benchmarks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot model policy API for enterprise, orgs, and teams
item.description:
GitHub added REST API support to retrieve and update Copilot model policies for enterprises, enterprise teams, enterprise apps, and organizations. The change introduces new GET and PATCH endpoints for managing these policies.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings enforcement updates
item.description:
Enterprise admins can now require supported GitHub Copilot clients to fetch current server-managed settings at startup rather than using cached policy. GitHub is also adding minimum client version enforcement.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now attribute GitHub Copilot activity to a user in managed settings without collecting prompts, responses, or tool content. A new telemetry.capture.identity setting provides configurable client telemetry capture options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in-product validator
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes an in-product validator for enterprise managed settings. It checks for malformed JSON, unsupported configurations, invalid team mappings, and similar issues that could block settings from working correctly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default Enablement of Copilot Features for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default policy that enables generally available Copilot features and supported client capabilities in enterprise and organization Copilot settings. The change takes effect over a 28-day window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review now supports more personal configuration options, is available to a broader set of Copilot plans, and adds an enterprise-level default setting. These changes are generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard now shows feature engagement
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes feature engagement data, showing how many active users regularly use key Copilot features. Enterprise administrators can use it to identify widely adopted experiences and those that may need more attention.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise admins can now centrally manage agent operation permissions. Admins can set operations to be blocked, require human approval, or run without prompting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed sandbox in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise-managed sandbox policies, along with cross-file cursor jumps for next edit suggestions, global project context in chat, and enterprise policy diagnostics. The update also adds a new terminal Copilot connection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusion policies set at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. Excluded files will not be used as context by Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Apps can now access enterprise billing data
item.description:
GitHub Apps can now be granted access to enterprise billing data by enterprise owners. The app configuration flow now includes an enterprise billing permission that can be selected when creating or updating an app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprises can now install third-party GitHub Apps
item.description:
Enterprise owners can now install public GitHub Apps built outside their enterprise on enterprise accounts. This enables third-party integrations for enterprise management scenarios.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Limit remote control to managed devices
item.description:
Enterprises and organizations can now limit Copilot remote control sessions to managed devices. This adds administrator control over which devices are eligible to host remote control access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default model enablement for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default enablement policy for generally available Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. New GA models will be enabled by default instead of requiring admins to turn each one on manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage GitHub Copilot app access with a dedicated policy
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now has a dedicated policy for controlling app access at both the enterprise and organization levels. This separates Copilot app access from the previous broader access controls.

  • Source: GitHub
